FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Reckless driving means operating a vehicle in a way that endangers people or property, whether or not it is intentional. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
If an officer sees your driving as endangering a person or property, including another vehicle, you can be charged under the reckless driving statute and face up to eight points on your record if convicted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Tailgating, passing on the shoulder or running a red light can be treated as aggressive when an officer believes it was willful and endangered others, and so can a mix of speeding, cutting off, swerving, honking, flashing lights, yelling and rude gestures. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Showing a weapon to another motorist, bumping or ramming a vehicle, or chasing a vehicle at high speed can bring criminal charges beyond reckless driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
To protect yourself from an aggressive driver, do not engage: avoid eye contact, do not respond in kind, back off and let the driver go. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A01
Report aggressive drivers by dialing *CSP (*277), a free Colorado State Patrol cellphone line for motorists and bicyclists that routes the call to the nearest trooper or a local agency. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A01
Anyone can become an aggressive driver; warning signs include insulting other drivers, blocking merges or passing, tailgating to push someone, angry speeding, running controls out of anger, honking or yelling, gestures, pursuing or ramming, getting out to confront, or thinking about attacking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A01
Answering yes to even a couple of the self-check questions means you may be at risk of becoming an aggressive driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A01
To avoid becoming aggressive, leave early, expect others to make mistakes, stay calm, keep anger from elsewhere out of your driving and let people merge even if they were rude. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A01
When a crash seems likely, many drivers panic, yet there is almost always something you can do to avoid it or lessen its results. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A01
The three ways to avoid a collision are to slow down or stop, to turn, or to speed up. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A01
To stop fast with anti-lock brakes, press hard and firmly and keep the pedal down even if it pushes back, since ABS works only while the pedal is pressed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A01
To stop fast without anti-lock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels; if they lock and you skid, ease off slightly, then brake again once the skid stops, repeating until stopped. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A01
You can usually turn a vehicle faster than you can stop it, so steer around a hazard if that will not cause another crash, gripping the wheel with both hands and staying ready to control the car afterward. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A01
Anti-lock brakes let you steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must turn and slow at once. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A02
Without anti-lock brakes, brake to slow somewhat, then release the brake before the evasive turn, and do not lock the front wheels or turn so sharply that the car only plows ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A02
Leaving the road is generally a better outcome than a head-on collision with another vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A02
Accelerating out of danger can be the answer when another vehicle is about to strike your side or rear and the road ahead is open; slow back down afterward. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A02
Watch for animals especially in rural and mountain areas and between dusk and dawn, when about 90% of deer and elk crashes happen, and slow down and look on entering a marked animal crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A02
A drastic swerve to miss a large animal can cause loss of control and a worse crash, so hitting the animal may be the safest choice; focus on keeping control before, during and after impact. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A02
Following the maintenance schedule in the owner's manual greatly reduces the chance of a vehicle failure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A02
If the brakes fail, lift off the gas and pump the pedal; if that fails, apply the parking brake slowly, ready to release it if you skid, then shift to lower gears, find a safe spot off the road and do not drive on without brakes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A02
In a tire blowout, grip the wheel tightly, keep going straight, take your foot off the gas, brake lightly and slow gradually, then pull off the road somewhere safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F24 | anchor: A02
If power fails, hold the wheel firmly and pull off the road; steering will be hard but possible, and the brakes still work with much harder pressure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F25 | anchor: A02
If headlights fail, pull off as soon as possible, try the switch a few times, and if that does not work use the emergency flashers, turn signals or fog lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F26 | anchor: A02
If the gas pedal jams, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral quickly, pull off when safe and turn off the engine. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F27 | anchor: A02
After a crash you must show proof of insurance to law enforcement, either at the scene or at the police station. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F28 | anchor: A02
If the driver cannot physically report an injury crash, a passenger must report it and, if law enforcement directs, stay at the scene until officers arrive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F29 | anchor: A02
After a crash, stop at once and never leave, check for injuries and give reasonable help where practical, call law enforcement and emergency services, and exchange names, addresses, phone numbers, registration and insurance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F30 | anchor: A02
During Accident Alert Status, when severe weather keeps officers from answering all crashes, drivers in a crash with no alcohol, drugs or injuries and drivable vehicles exchange information and must file a report within 24 hours. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F31 | anchor: A02
If you hit a parked car and cannot find its owner, call law enforcement and leave a note where the owner will find it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F32 | anchor: A02
Under the Move It Law, after a minor divided-highway crash with drivable vehicles and no injuries, drugs or alcohol, drivers must get the vehicles off the highway, and police and insurers will not penalize them for it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec15-F33 | anchor: A03
The Move Over Law requires moving over one lane, when safe, for any stopped vehicle on a highway with hazards flashing; if that is unsafe or the road has one lane each way, slow to at least 20 mph under the posted limit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec15-F34 | anchor: A03
Good Samaritan laws encourage helping in emergencies and expect common sense and reasonable skill within your training; acting as a reasonable, prudent person generally protects a rescuer from being sued and held financially responsible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec15-F35 | anchor: A03
A reasonable rescuer moves a victim only if life is in danger, asks a conscious victim before helping, checks for life-threatening problems first, calls for professional help and keeps giving care until trained help arrives. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec15-F36 | anchor: A03
When applying for or renewing a license, permit or ID you are asked whether to register as an organ, eye and tissue donor; a yes puts a heart with a Y on the card and adds you to the Donate Life Colorado registry until you change it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec15-F37 | anchor: A03
You are also asked whether to make a voluntary gift to the organ and tissue donation awareness fund named for Emily Keyes and John W. Buckner, which pays for public outreach and education. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0030]
